segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל הַבָּשָׂר אָסוּר לְבַשֵּׁל בְּחָלָב, חוּץ מִבְּשַׂר דָּגִים וַחֲגָבִים, וְאָסוּר לְהַעֲלוֹת עִם הַגְּבִינָה עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן, חוּץ מִבְּשַׂר דָּגִים וַחֲגָבִים.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» It is «prohibited to cook any meat» of domesticated and undomesticated animals and birds «in milk, except for the meat of fish and grasshoppers,» whose halakhic status is not that of meat. «And» likewise, the Sages issued a decree that it is «prohibited to place» any meat together «with» milk products, e.g., «cheese, on» one «table.» The reason for this prohibition is that one might come to eat them after they absorb substances from each other. This prohibition applies to all types of meat, «except for the meat of fish and grasshoppers.»

segments.he: הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הַבָּשָׂר מוּתָּר בִּבְשַׂר דָּגִים וַחֲגָבִים.
segments.en: And «one who takes a vow» that «meat» is prohibited to him is «permitted to» eat «the meat of fish and grasshoppers.»

moves.summary: the chapter-closing formula ending Gid HaNasheh
the mishna forbids cooking any meat in milk and placing meat with cheese on one table, excepting fish and grasshoppers
the mishna adds that one who vows from meat is permitted the flesh of fish and grasshoppers
